source_text: {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Δέχεται τοίνυν εἰς παράδειγμα τοῦ μὴ διχηλοῦντος μὲν τὴν ὁπλὴν, ἀνακομίζοντος δὲ τὸν μηρυκισμὸν, τὴν κάμηλον, ζῶον εὐσθενές τε καὶ ὑπερμέγεθες, δασύποδά τε καὶ χοιρογρύλλιον, τὰ πάντων, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, τῶν ἄλλων μικροφανέστατα, διὰ τῶν ἄκρων, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, συλλήβδην ἅπαντα περιλαβὼν, καὶ οὐδὲν ἔξω τῶν διὰ μέσου μεθείς. Ὅμοιον γὰρ ὡς εἰ καὶ λέγοιτο τυχὸν, Ἀπὸ τοῦ λίαν ὑψηλοῦ τε καὶ ἀνωτάτω καὶ μέχρι μικρῶν, καὶ τῶν ὅτι μάλιστα κατωτάτω, πᾶς ὅς γε τοιοῦτος βδελυρὸς καὶ ἀκάθαρτος. Οὐ γάρ ἐστι
pass_a_gloss: §20 dual gloss: προσωποληψία / face-taking · χοιρογρύλλιος / porcupine · θεογνωσία / God-knowledge … Pass A scaffolding ≠ Pass B continuous English. Theme: Camel/hare/pig types; works without piety dead; water-creatures begin.
pass_b_english: Cyril: So then he receives unto an example of the not splitting on the one hand the hoof, yet bringing-back the rumination, the camel, an animal both well-strong and over-great, and rough-foot and porcupine, the most small-appearing as a word to say of all the others, through the extremes, as I at least think, having embraced all together, and having released nothing outside of the through the middle. For like as if somehow it should also be said, From the very high and uppermost and until small ones, and of the as much as most lowest, every who at least such is abominable and unclean. For there is not face-taking beside God, according to the having-been-written; but whether someone should be great and haughty, having been lifted unto height with wealth and glory the according to world, he will carry-away the unfamed and unprized vote, being held in the charges of worthlessness; or whether someone should be small, living-with poverty and unglory, he will be condemned toward uncleanness, if he should not boast in the manners unto virtue; nor would someone make a find of the lowliness, the needing to be pitied beside the just Judge, not having the well-fitting in works, clear that the according to piety and virtue. So then a camel on the one hand, and a hare and a porcupine, would be a not unclear type of small and great. And he also brings-beside the swine, as unclean, through at least the splitting on the one hand a hoof, yet not still also having been natural also to chew-up nourishment, that is, to bring-up rumination, showing strengthless and useless the boast in works, without the word the according to piety. For just as the faith without the works is dead, so also the reverse, somehow altogether dead the good-order, and the fair in works, with God-knowledge being absent, and with word the according to piety not having house-dwelt in our souls, and being below, it has nodded-in unto earth, and somehow seems to fear the raising-up above the eye. Some such having suffered we will find not few, who sometimes have a reverend and clean life, yet not having recognized God the by nature and true, as it were somehow only fix the eye of the mind upon the upon the earth. And unclean also such again; ‘For no one is crowned, if he should not contend lawfully,’ according to the having-been-written.
Palladius: So then it defiles us as in a form of a swine, and indeed also of the others, those having been borne-under the slanders from law.

Cyril: Very much so you spoke rightly. And it is not sufficient for the law to bring-beside the images of the unclean, and through at least only also of such somehow, but through as it were all the creation having chosen to benefit us and setting-beside richly the knowledge of the useful and fitting, it also goes-through the kinds of water-ones, and herds of winged ones, in order that busying very well the having grown for each, what on the one hand thereafter would be the pleasing God, and what rejectable and having been hated by him we may have to think-around
